 Hornets Show Signs of Life
 BenJammin G 
 November 17, 2026 
 5:00 am 
 64 Comments 
 Editor’s Note: Ben wrote this prior to the Clippers game. 
 The Hornets won in near blowout fashion versus the Cavaliers, then lost a close game versus playoff-aspiring Phoenix. Against the Cavs, the Hornets played well on both sides of the court, draining threes, securing the ball, and playing tough defense. Then, in Phoenix, rebounding and defense gave the Hornets a lead for much of the game, but ball handling slip-ups and passing errors gave the Phoenix offense room run and win it in the end.
 A Recurring Problem
 Killing lapses in ball control highlighted the team’s weak point, and it cost them the game, again, exacerbated by Coby’s minute restriction and Schröder’s hamstrung absence. Sion played point guard minutes, Grayson too, who at one point led a disastrous one guard, four big lineup that absolutely hurt to watch. Grayson may, just barely, have enough ball handling and passing to play point guard in a pinch, but only if playing alongside other ball handling guards and forwards, who work together every possession to advance the ball and start offense.
 Help On The Way
 The Hornets need help at point guard, and with ball handling and passing team-wide. Luckily, help is on the way. Rookie speedster Christian Anderson powered the Hornets offense during his playing time, confidently draining three of six threes. They weren’t all easy takes. His ball handling and purpose on offensive leveled up compared to his first games. Two assists with two turnovers is sub-par for a backup point guard, and he snared no rebounds, but a potent three-point shot can cover for a lot of flaws, and he looked the part of a decent PG2, including showing a pesky defensive game that shined a light on his athleticism. But, what do we him? CA works, but is blah. Chris-A? C-Andy, heh? He has rapidly progressed from the over-whelmed and over-matched ultra green rookie they saw at first.
 Sion, for all his flaws as a scorer and primary or secondary ball handler, was +2 in 32 minutes versus Phoenix: his defense an essential part of a winning recipe. He’s developing as a ball handler and assist man, though it’s painful to watch sometimes. With experience and practice, he’ll improve. He’s showed notable improvement handling the ball this year compared to last, with a quicker and more decisive dribble. He passed for 6 assists last night: if he cut his turnovers, then we’d have a good chance of winning the game. The same can be said of every other starter, who had four turnovers apiece. Grayson was the only one beside Sion who mustered a positive assist/turnover ratio with a passable six assists as well.
 Booker is a tough match for anyone and Sion didn’t exactly shine on defense like he did the other night versus Mitchell, but Sion did alright versus another legit star combo guard with superior length, athleticism and skill level.
 Grant Williams returned to the court and performed well, lifting the second string with quality two-way play including making two of four threes, a block, and, crucially, no turnovers. Coby also looked more himself: still not shooting well from three point range, but he scored effectively in the paint and midrange, showing his trademark speed, quickness and bucket-making ability. But, his availability, at only 20 minutes, was a problem for the team, as were his four turnovers with only three assists. As these two players get their legs under them and eventually emerge from restricted minutes, they will both be stalwarts of the rotation.
 The Prospects for the Future of the Franchise
 When the Hornets get them back, Brandon and Kon will elevate the team greatly, on both offense and defense, especially once they are back in game shape and find rhythm and chemistry within new lineups. Last year, as very young semi-stars on a winning team, they posted 3.4 and 3.3 assists per game, respectively, with modestly positive assist to turnover ratios. Not bad. Unfortunately, Kon will likely be recovering for another month from that hamstring injury, which are notoriously tough to shake.
 This Hornets’ roster is a transitory thing. Though many of the players will be Hornets for years to come, the build is incomplete. They have good young players under contract: keepers like Kon, Brandon, Coby, and Moussa, valuable rotation players: Reid, Kalk, Sion, and quality developing young depth: Tidjane, Hannes, C-Andy, Liam, as well as great veteran leadership in Grant and Grayson plus two other solid veterans in Royce and Schröder. Maybe, before long, the Hornets will be able to move Naz over to the keepers category, and count Tidjane, C-Andy, and Hannes as valuable rotation-level players. The Hornets’ injury problems have provided all three of those college-age kids with valuable minutes in the rotation.
 Even with their top two players out versus Phoenix, and missing their backup point guard, the Hornets were close to pulling off an upset on the road, based on their defense, rebounding and three point shooting. Those are good, stout pillars to build a team around. This roster has talent: built to improve internally for years to come, to compete now, if healthy, and to have massive flexibility for upgrades, given our big draft pick stash, the team’s numerous tradable contracts and their traded-player exceptions, including the monster $40.77 million LaMelo exception, and the $8.2 million Sexton exception.
 Can They Level Up This Year?
 Coby, the last time he started at point guard in Chicago, played beside LaVine, DeRozan and Vučević: stars who all play-make with the ball in their hands as their primary skill in the NBA, so this is Coby’s first time as the clear stand-alone primary ball handler at starting point guard. The Hornets likely envision him as a score-first PG who posts something like 6 assists 2.5 turnovers per game. He faces a sizable learning curve as he adapts to being the man with the ball in his hands on most possessions and as he learns new lineups. The Hornets can expect improvement from him, as he gains experience in that role and builds on his years of experience as a starting combo-guard.
 Chris-A is easing worries about point guard depth with his improved play, and while we can expect rookie growing pains, he does look like he belongs in the league now and will be improving over the course of the year. Schröder also contributes important depth at point guard and he’ll be back in time.
 If/when Coby, Brandon and Kon all get healthy at once, stretch the floor and attack close-outs, this team will look completely different than it has so far, even if ball handling still won’t be a team strength. Kon and Brandon are both versatile players who can dribble, pass, shoot, and defend, and they bring decent size to the wing spots for us. Hornets fans should not forget how much better Charlotte is with those two rising stars on the court.
